newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: BP eyes new opportunities in Mexico, Brazil.
newsitem.headline: BP eyes new opportunities in Mexico, Brazil.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc is carefully eyeing opportunities for expansion into Brazil and Mexico, its head of Latin American operations said.

In a Reuter interview, John Doust, president of BP's Colombia unit BP Exploration (BPX) and regional chief, said he was optimistic the Mexican oil sector -- at present heavily controlled by the state -- would open up to the private sector.
"In addition to further establishing our positions in Colombia and Venezuela, we're looking at the big economies of Brazil and Mexico which are interesting places for BP Exploration," Doust said.
"I imagine things will open up in the coming years in Mexico. We have a small office there and want to maintain contact and build relations there," he added.

Mexico's oil industry was nationalized in 1938. A bid to sell off the state-run secondary petrochemical industry failed last year amid heated, nationalistic debate and a revised formula was produced to allow only minority private sector participation.
But Doust was hopeful Mexico would eventually open up all sectors of the oil industry to private participation, including exploration, production and refining.
"I don't think Mexico has really made up its mind yet about what it wants. But hopefully something will materialize and we want to be part of that," he said.
